stem:
Amino acids are molecules that contain $-\text{NH}_2$ and $-\text{COOH}$ functional groups.

Glycine, $\text{H}_2\text{NCH}_2\text{COOH}$, is the simplest stable amino acid.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem: The isoelectric point of glycine is 6.2.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Draw the structure of glycine at pH4.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: State the essential conditions for reaction 1.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Identify the reagent used in reaction 2.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Draw the structure of the organic product **U** that forms when hippuric acid reacts with an excess of $\text{LiAlH}_4$ in reaction 3.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
(c)(i)
parts.stem:
A student proposes a synthesis of hippuric acid by the reaction of benzamide, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CONH}_2$, and chloroethanoic acid, $\text{ClCH}_2\text{COOH}$.

The reaction does **not** work well because benzamide is a very weak base.
parts.text: Explain why amides are weaker bases than amines.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The $pK_a$ of chloroethanoic acid is 2.86 whereas the $pK_a$ of ethanoic acid is 4.76.

Explain the difference between these two $pK_a$ values.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
Compound **V** is another amino acid.

The proton ($^1\text{H}$) NMR spectrum of **V** shows hydrogen atoms in five different environments, **a**, **b**, **c**, **d** and **e**, as shown in Fig. 6.2.

{{figure:pdf_visual_04.png}}

Fig. 6.2

Table 6.1

| environment of proton | example | chemical shift range, $\delta$/ppm |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| alkane | $-\text{CH}_3$, $-\text{CH}_2-$, $>\text{CH}-$ | 0.9-1.7 |
| alkyl next to C=O | $\text{CH}_3-\text{C=O}$, $-\text{CH}_2-\text{C=O}$, $>\text{CH}-\text{C=O}$ | 2.2-3.0 |
| alkyl next to aromatic ring | $\text{CH}_3-\text{Ar}$, $-\text{CH}_2-\text{Ar}$, $>\text{CH}-\text{Ar}$ | 2.3-3.0 |
| alkyl next to electronegative atom | $\text{CH}_3-\text{O}$, $-\text{CH}_2-\text{O}$, $-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl}$, $-\text{CH}_2-\text{N}$ | 3.2-4.0 |
| attached to alkene | $=\text{CHR}$ | 4.5-6.0 |
| attached to aromatic ring | $\text{H}-\text{Ar}$ | 6.0-9.0 |
| aldehyde | $\text{HCOR}$ | 9.3-10.5 |
| alcohol | $\text{ROH}$ | 0.5-6.0 |
| phenol | $\text{Ar}-\text{OH}$ | 4.5-7.0 |
| carboxylic acid | $\text{RCOOH}$ | 9.0-13.0 |
| alkyl amine | $\text{R}-\text{NH}-$ | 1.0-5.0 |
| aryl amine | $\text{Ar}-\text{NH}_2$ | 3.0-6.0 |
| amide | $\text{RCONHR}$ | 5.0-12.0 |
